talentsSkipWildcards.Name: Talents skip wildcard skills
talentsSkipWildcards.Hint: A Talent adds nothing to a wildcard skill, even one covering the skills on its list (Monster Hunters 1 p. 24).

holyAttacks.Name: Holy attacks
holyAttacks.Hint: Contact with holy water or a holy weapon burns a creature with a Weakness to holy things for 1d, ignoring DR, then fizzes for a minute in which no holy source hurts it again (Monster Hunters 1 p. 51).

ritualPathMagic.Name: Ritual Path Magic
ritualPathMagic.Hint: Magic as nine IQ/Very Hard Path skills, each held to the lower of Thaumatology and 12 + Magery and defaulting to Thaumatology-6 (no higher than 12), with a mana reserve of Magery x 3. Magery no longer adds to Thaumatology (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 24, 32-39).

monsterHuntersGear.Name: Monster Hunters gear
monsterHuntersGear.Hint: Gadgets and clothing take improvements priced by cost factor (cutting-edge, disguised, rugged, good and fine quality, scent-masking, undercover), and Signature Gear costs a point per $10,000 of each item (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 53-54, 59).

bonusPointSpending.Name: Destiny and wildcard points
bonusPointSpending.Hint: Destiny points and wildcard bonus points join unspent points in buying successes, flesh wounds and player guidance; the GM starts each session to refresh them (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 23, 28, 31).

MH1.TalentSkipsWildcard: Talents never add to wildcard skills (Monster Hunters 1 p. 24)
MH1.DestinyHint: Spent as bonus character points; one regained each session, never more than you started with (Monster Hunters 1 p. 23).
MH1.WildcardHint: One bonus point per 12 points in the wildcard skill, handed out each session; they don't accumulate, and pay only for that skill's rolls (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 28, 31).
MH1.GmDestinyHint: A negative Destiny: the GM sets these aside each session to spend against you (Monster Hunters 1 p. 23).
MH1.FullyTrainedHint: 12+ points in a wildcard skill: ignore penalties for familiarity, exotic equipment and tech level differences, but not improvised or low-quality gear (Monster Hunters 1 p. 28).
MH1.NewSessionHint: Hand out wildcard bonus points, regain a destiny point, and set aside the GM's destiny points (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 23, 28).
MH1.WildcardOnlyItsSkill: Wildcard bonus points pay only for that skill's rolls.
MH1.NotEnough: Not enough points in that pool.

Holy.Title: Holy attack
Holy.Burns: {name} is burned by {source}: {injury} injury, ignoring DR ({from} → {to} HP). It fizzes for a minute.
Holy.Fizzing: {name} is still fizzing from the last burn: {source} does nothing for another {seconds} s.
Holy.Rule: 1d ignoring DR, then a minute in which no holy source does more (Monster Hunters 1 p. 51).
Holy.ContactHint: Touch whoever is targeted with this: a creature with a Weakness to holy things takes 1d, ignoring DR, unless it is still fizzing (Monster Hunters 1 p. 51).
Holy.NoTarget: Target who is being touched with it first.
Holy.NoEffect: Nobody targeted is hurt by holy things, or all of them are still fizzing.
Holy.CannotApply: You can't change {name}: ask the GM to apply the holy contact.

Ritual.MasteryHint: +2 to all Path skill rolls for this ritual (Monster Hunters 1 p. 25).
Ritual.MasteryChangedHint: The definition has changed since it was mastered: it counts as a different ritual (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
Ritual.RecordMasteryHint: Record this definition as the one Ritual Mastery is for.
Ritual.BlockingHint: The GM agrees this ritual makes sense as an out-of-turn defense: it is offered on attacks as a blocking spell (Monster Hunters 1 p. 37).
Ritual.Title: Rituals
Ritual.Hint: Written down once, with what each costs and the Path it is rolled against (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 33-35).
Ritual.CostHint: (Spell effects + modifiers) x Greater effects multiplier, less any traditional trappings (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 33-34).
Ritual.PathPenaltyHint: -1 to every roll for each Path past the second (Monster Hunters 1 p. 35).
Ritual.DurationConflictHint: Damage and healing cannot be combined with a duration (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).
Ritual.NoEffects: No effects yet: a ritual needs at least one.
Ritual.DefinitionHint: What makes this ritual this one: change any of it and Ritual Mastery or a grimoire no longer applies (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
Ritual.AfflictionPercentHint: +1 energy for every +5% the affliction is worth as an enhancement to Affliction; stunning costs nothing (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).

DamageKind.label: Damage priced as
DamageKind.heavy: Corrosion, fatigue, huge piercing or impaling (x2)

Ritual.TraitsAddedHint: +1 energy per character point of advantages or attributes added, or disadvantages reduced (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).
Ritual.TraitsRemovedHint: +1 energy per 5 character points of disadvantages added, or attributes or advantages reduced (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).
Ritual.MetaMagicHint: Dispelling or altering magic costs the energy of the original spell (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).
Ritual.YearsHint: For durations over a year, the added energy is the number of years + 21 (Monster Hunters 1 p. 35).
Ritual.SubjectWeightHint: For a physical change, the weight of the largest single subject, not of them all (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).
Ritual.TrappingsHint: The GM's discount of up to 25% for cool, flavourful embellishments (Monster Hunters 1 p. 34).

RitualPath.Title: Ritual Path Magic
RitualPath.CeilingHint: No Path skill may exceed the lower of Thaumatology and 12 + Magery (Monster Hunters 1 p. 32).
RitualPath.AdeptHint: Gathers in seconds rather than minutes, with none of the non-adept penalties (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 25, 36).
RitualPath.NonAdeptHint: Gathering takes minutes, and connection, consecrated space and lacking Magery each cost -5 (Monster Hunters 1 p. 36).
RitualPath.ReserveHint: Magery x 3 points of energy, drawn on in a second; refilled with Path of Magic, and assumed full after downtime (Monster Hunters 1 p. 36).

RitualCast.ExtendTooLong: An extension cannot lengthen a ritual by more than its original duration.
RitualCast.Stacking: Shares {effects} with {other}: on the same subject, only {survivor} remains (the one that took more energy).
RitualCast.Defused: {name} is defused without effect: no more than {limit} conditional rituals can hang at once.
RitualCast.Hanging: Hanging until its condition is met ({count} of {limit}).
RitualCast.Triggered: {source}: it goes off with its original margin of {margin}.
RitualCast.TriggerWaiting: {name}'s player or the GM starts it on their sheet.
RitualCast.NotYours: {name}'s mana reserve is not yours to draw on: their player or the GM can.
RitualCast.RefillNotYours: {name}'s mana reserve refills to {max}, for their player or the GM to top off.
RitualCast.CannotCancelConditional: A conditional ritual cannot be cancelled by its caster; the GM can remove it.
RitualCast.Conditional: Cast conditionally (it hangs until the condition is met)
RitualCast.ConditionPlaceholder: The condition, e.g. anyone but us enters the room
RitualCast.BreakHint: A Ready maneuver: the object breaks and its ritual goes off with its original margin (Monster Hunters 1 p. 38).
RitualCast.BreakConfirm: Break {item}? It is destroyed and its ritual goes off.
RitualCast.UseGrimoireHint: Read from the grimoire: its bonus to every roll, and all casting times doubled (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
RitualCast.JoinHint: Target the characters working this ritual together. Each adds their energy, and every roll is at -1 per caster past the first (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
RitualCast.CannotJoin: {name} cannot work this ritual: no Path within reach.
RitualCast.Blocked: Blocked: the ritual works in time, and counts as the active defense.
RitualCast.BlockFailed: The ritual isn't quick enough to work.
RitualCast.BlockingNote: A blocking ritual, at most once per turn: instant gathering at -10, tapping at -5. A caster who fails gets no other active defense unless using All-Out Defense (Double Defense) (Monster Hunters 1 p. 37).
RitualCast.Connected: Connected to the subject (present, located, or something of theirs)
RitualCast.AdeptTimes: Working at an adept's speed (-5, and tapping needs a roll)
RitualCast.DesecratedHint: Desecrated ground produces no ambient energy; only sources can be tapped.
RitualCast.GatheredQuick: gathered {energy}, and the next attempt takes one second
RitualCast.GatheredQuirk: gathered {energy}, and the spell picks up a quirk
RitualCast.Backfire: the ritual fails horribly. The GM turns {energy} energy against the caster and friends.
RitualCast.TapFailed: the source could not be tapped
RitualCast.Abandoned: Abandoned with {energy} energy gathered; it is released harmlessly.
RitualCast.Retry: the energy doesn't flow. Concentrate {seconds} more seconds, then try again.
RitualCast.Cast: the ritual works, by a margin of {margin}
RitualCast.InformationRolled: The GM rolled the final roll in secret.
RitualCast.InformationRolledRetry: The GM rolled in secret: the energy did not flow. Try again.
RitualCast.InformationRetry: a failure: the caster must try again
RitualCast.InformationLie: failed by 5 or more: the GM lies
RitualCast.ReservePrompt: Energy to draw ({reserve} in the reserve)
RitualCast.NoDonors: Everyone here has already given to this ritual.
RitualCast.NoEffects: This ritual has no effects to cast.
RitualCast.Uncastable: {path} is out of reach: this ritual cannot be worked.
RitualCast.CannotApply: You do not have permission to change: {names}
RitualCast.MageryOffThaumatology: Magery doesn't add to Thaumatology under Ritual Path Magic (Monster Hunters 1 p. 24)
RitualCast.PathCapped: Held to the lower of Thaumatology and 12 + Magery (Monster Hunters 1 p. 33)
RitualCast.PathDefault: Thaumatology-6, no higher than 12 (Monster Hunters 1 p. 33)
RitualCast.SwitchOff: Ritual Path Magic is switched off in the Rules settings.
RitualCast.NotYourCard: Only the GM, or the player who started this casting, can move it on.

Grimoire.Title: Grimoire
Grimoire.Hint: Add the rituals this book teaches to make it a grimoire (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
Grimoire.ChangedHint: The ritual's definition has changed since it was chosen, so this book no longer teaches it (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39). Choose it again to rebind.
Grimoire.DeadLanguageHint: Full bonus for Native comprehension, -1 for Accented, half for Broken, none without it or a translation (Monster Hunters 1 p. 39).
Grimoire.Price: As a new book: ${cost}, {weight} lbs. (Monster Hunters 1 p. 57)

Gadget.Title: Improvements
Gadget.CuttingEdgeHint: The latest materials: weight x2/3, +1 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 54).
Gadget.DisguisedHint: Resembles something else of a similar shape; finding it out takes a Search roll, or Observation in plain sight. +4 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 54).
Gadget.RuggedHint: Shockproof and waterproof: +2 on rolls to avoid breakage and water damage, weight x1.2, +1 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 54).
Gadget.ScentMaskingHint: -4 to Smell rolls to find or track the wearer. +2 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 59).
Gadget.UndercoverHint: Helps conceal weapons: +1 Holdout for +4 CF, +2 for +19 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 59).
Gadget.HoldoutHint: The Holdout bonus the article gives of itself; Undercover adds to it.
Gadget.Priced: Cost factor +{cf}, weight x{weight}, from a list price of ${cost} and {listWeight} lbs. Good and fine quality add +4 and +19 CF, except on tool kits and labs.
Gadget.SignatureHint: Each item marked as Signature Gear costs 1 point for every $10,000 or fraction of its price (Monster Hunters 1 p. 53).
Gadget.SmellNote: {penalty} to Smell rolls to find them
Gadget.ListCostHint: The table's price before improvements; left at 0, the item's own price is the list price (Monster Hunters 1 p. 54).
Gadget.ListWeightHint: The table's weight before improvements; left at 0, the item's own weight is the list weight.

WeaponImprovement.BalancedHint: +1 to skill with the weapon. +4 CF; not for sticks (Monster Hunters 1 p. 59).
WeaponImprovement.TitaniumHint: Weight x3/4 and -2 to odds of breakage, not cumulative with fine or very fine. +1 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
WeaponImprovement.WeightedHint: +1 damage. Two-handed axes and maces only: +1 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
WeaponImprovement.CompoundHint: ST+2 for damage and range. +1 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
WeaponImprovement.ImprovisedHint: An improvised weapon's skill penalty, e.g. -1 for a pool cue; Improvised Weapons for the skill removes it (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 25, 60).
WeaponImprovement.Priced: Cost factor +{cf} from a list price of ${cost} and {weight} lbs. Fine is free; very fine +3 CF (swords and fencing weapons); silver +19; silver-coated +2; holy +4, at least $250 (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 59-61).

Problem.veryFineNotSword: Very fine is for swords and fencing weapons only (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
Problem.silverCombination: Silver cannot be combined with fine, very fine or titanium (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
Problem.weightedNotTwoHandedAxe: Weighted is for two-handed axes and maces only (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
Problem.compoundNotBow: Compound is for bows and crossbows only (Monster Hunters 1 p. 60).
Problem.cheapNotOffered: Monster Hunters gear has no cheap grade; the weapon is priced as good (Monster Hunters 1 p. 59).

SpecialAmmo.PowderHint: One powder option per load (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
SpecialAmmo.PayloadHint: One payload option per load. Shotgun payloads fire as slugs, except silver (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
SpecialAmmo.MagazineHint: An empty magazine or speedloader's price. Special ammunition's CF multiplies the rounds, not this (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
SpecialAmmo.HandLoadHint: An Armoury (Small Arms) roll per asterisked option, with a reloading press: success -2 CF, failure +2 CF (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
SpecialAmmo.HandLoadGood: {option}: rolled {roll} vs {level}, a good batch (-2 CF)
SpecialAmmo.FollowUpHint: The load's follow-up attack; roll it after the bullet (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).

Problem.shotgunOnly: That payload is for shotguns only (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
Problem.notShotgun: That payload is for pistols, rifles and SMGs, not shotguns (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
Problem.dragonsBreathPowder: Dragon's Breath cannot be combined with any powder option (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).

NoteHint.silent: Greatly reduces the odds of being heard: -5 to Hearing Shots (Monster Hunters 1 pp. 61, 63).
NoteHint.smoke: Releases smoke in a 4-yard radius for 20 seconds on impact (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63; Campaigns p. 439).
NoteHint.tearGas: Releases tear gas in a 4-yard radius for 20 seconds on impact (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63; Campaigns p. 439).
NoteHint.dragonsBreath: A cone 75 yards long and 10 yards wide at the end. The gun cannot fire again for three seconds (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
NoteHint.explosive: If the slug penetrates DR, the follow-up damage is tripled and ignores DR. +1 to Hearing Shots (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
NoteHint.flare: Shot into the air, it lights a 50-yard radius for 20 seconds; darkness there is no worse than -3 (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
NoteHint.rockSalt: No damage. Living things and zombies roll HT+DR or suffer moderate pain for minutes equal to the margin of failure; salt ignores zombies' High Pain Threshold. A failed roll after a shot to the face destroys a zombie (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
NoteHint.silver: Solid silver: wounds what silver wounds (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).
NoteHint.wooden: A shot to the heart counts as a stake for vampires (Monster Hunters 1 p. 63).

Migration.Done: Monster Hunters 1: moved the book's data from the system into this module ({changed} changes).
Migration.Failed: Monster Hunters 1: {failed} documents could not be moved into this module. The steps that failed run again the next time the world loads; see the console for which.

powerstones.Name: Powerstones
powerstones.Hint: A stone's capacity prices it, it recharges by the mana where it is, and a carried stone can pay for a spell in place of fatigue: a One-College stone for its college, a dedicated or exclusive one for its item's spells.

spellAttacks.Name: Jets, breaths and rains
spellAttacks.Hint: A Regular spell whose record declares an attack rolls it as it is cast and each turn it lasts, dodged or blocked but not parried; an Area spell's damage falls each second on everyone in the area, halved for less than a whole second.

Powerstone.Title: Powerstones
Powerstone.IsStoneHint: An object holding mana a wizard can spend in place of his own energy
Powerstone.SetIntoHint: The magic item whose spells this stone pays for, by name
Powerstone.PricedHint: An ordinary stone's price follows its capacity, by the table in Magic
Powerstone.RechargeHint: Adds what the mana here gives back for the world time passed since the last recharge. Of the stones a character carries, only the largest recharge.

SpellAttack.AttackHint: This turn's attack: rolled against the spell's Innate Attack skill, dodged or blocked but not parried
SpellAttack.RainHint: Rolls the spell's damage for the creatures in the area to take through the damage card, with armor protecting as usual. No attack roll and no defense.
SpellAttack.RainPartial: Less than a whole second in the area (half)
SpellAttack.NoDamage: {spell} does what its description says; roll it by hand

committedDefensiveAttack.Name: Committed and Defensive Attack
committedDefensiveAttack.Hint: Two maneuvers between Attack and the All-Out ones. Committed Attack: +2 to hit or +1 damage, a second step at -2, and defenses at -2 with no retreat. Defensive Attack: -2 damage, or -1 per die, for +1 to a defense or an unbalanced weapon that can still parry.

allOutAttackOptions.Name: All-Out Attack (Long) and slams
allOutAttackOptions.Hint: All-Out Attack (Long): a yard more reach, swings at -2 damage or -1 per die, and a DX roll to end in a crouch. A slam, flying tackle, pounce or shield rush may take All-Out Attack at full Move with Determined, Feint or Strong.

moveAndAttack.Name: Move and Attack with any melee attack
moveAndAttack.Hint: Move and Attack allows a parry with what didn't strike. There is no retreat, no dodge after a kick or bite, no block with a shield that struck, and no Rapid Strike or Deceptive Attack, and a thrust may use slam damage where that is better.

acrobatics.Name: Acrobatics in combat
acrobatics.Hint: Acrobatic Stand from the ground; movement stunts (banister sliding, skidding, spinning, swinging, tic-tacs, tumbling, vaulting) that make the next dodge +2 or -2; and Acrobatic and Flying Attacks as Move and Attack.

postures.Name: Postures, hit locations and techniques
postures.Hint: Each posture's hit location effects, prohibited attacks and modified attacks, on top of the usual posture and location modifiers; and dropping to kneeling, crawling, prone, sitting or face-up as part of an attack.

feints.Name: Beats, Ruses and defensive feints
feints.Hint: A feint may be made as a Beat against one defense or a Ruse on IQ, or turned on the foe's next attack. Anyone resists with their best combat skill or a Feint technique, and Evaluate offsets feints and Deceptive Attacks from the evaluated foe.

readying.Name: Readying weapons
readying.Hint: Multiple Fast-Draw at -2 per earlier draw with the hand, Fast-Draw from odd positions and carry locations, a Ready that combines drawing with a grip change, rapid grip changes, and quick-readying a weapon from the floor, a rack or the ground.

meleeOptions.Name: Grips, Pummeling, Tip Slash and Telegraphic Attack
meleeOptions.Hint: Defensive Grip and half-swording, Reversed Grip with its forearm parry, Pummeling and Tip Slash as attack modes, and Telegraphic Attack. A weapon's grip is set by a Ready in the Readying section.

styles.Name: Styles and Style Familiarity
styles.Hint: Whether a character knows each style they have Style Familiarity for, and their Style Perk allowance, on the Skills tab (warnings only). Style Familiarity with every style a foe knows takes 1 off his feints and Deceptive Attacks.

training.Name: Training equipment and The Training Sequence
training.Hint: A character's training equipment adds to Teaching rolls, and a GM tool runs The Training Sequence for a master and students.

weaponBuilding.Name: Weapon balance, custom quality, combination and hidden weapons
weaponBuilding.Hint: Balance and custom quality levels, combination-weapon accessories with their attack modes, and concealment (rigs, trick weapons, special clothing, disguises) on a weapon's item sheet, priced in the book's order. Holdout and trick-weapon buttons on the weapon's row.

finerHitLocations.Name: New hit locations
finerHitLocations.Hint: Ear, jaw, joints, nose, spine, and veins and arteries as called shots, the skull and face from behind, crushing blows at the vitals, the 1d sub-rolls on random hits, and the lasting results of an ear, nose, spine or joint wound for the GM to confirm.

multipleAttacks.Name: Multiple attacks
multipleAttacks.Hint: Attacks from the maneuver and Extra Attack (All-Out Attack (Double) adds one), a Rapid Strike option applied to every attack in it, one special option per maneuver, a target picked per attack with an attack used up per yard skipped, feints traded for attacks, and no grappling move repeated on the same foe in a turn.

cinematicRapidStrike.Name: Cinematic Rapid Strike
cinematicRapidStrike.Hint: A Rapid Strike may have more than two attacks, at -6 per attack past the first on each (halved with Trained by a Master or Weapon Master). The GM may reserve it for those advantages, or cap adjusted skill at 12.

defenseOptions.Name: Active defense options
defenseOptions.Hint: Cross Parry and Supported Parry, Dive, Sideslip and Slip, Riposte, leg parries, a long two-handed weapon's parry against both halves of a Dual-Weapon Attack, and the fencing and two-handed refinements to multiple parries.

limitedDefenses.Name: Limits on dodging and blocking
limitedDefenses.Hint: -1 per dodge after the first in a turn, more than one block at -5 each (less for a Weapon Master), and dodging firearms only with evasive movement against the shooter. Trained by a Master and Weapon Master fighters are exempt from the dodge limits, as the book recommends.

targetedAttacks.Name: Targeted Attacks and Combinations
targetedAttacks.Hint: Techniques named TA (Skill Attack/Target) and Combination (A + B + C) work out their levels, ceilings and costs; an attack aimed where a TA aims takes its bought levels; Combinations run from the Combat tab; combat techniques also default to Art and Sport skills.

extraEffort.Name: Extra effort in combat
extraEffort.Hint: Giant Step, Great Lunge, Heroic Charge and Rapid Recovery; one offensive and one defensive extra-effort option a turn; Flurry of Blows a point of FP per Rapid Strike attack, halved again; Mighty Blows on Attack only; a critical failure on a new option costs 1 HP.

rangedOptions.Name: Ranged attack options
rangedOptions.Hint: Quick-shooting bows, blowpipes and slings; Rapid Strike and handfuls of thrown weapons; prediction shots that lower Dodge; feints at range; a Heroic Archer's extra aim.

cinematicRangedOptions.Name: Cinematic ranged options
cinematicRangedOptions.Hint: Quick-shooting in combat without the realistic -4, and handfuls of BL/20 lbs. of any small thrown weapon.

unfamiliarWeapons.Name: Unfamiliar weapons
unfamiliarWeapons.Hint: Weapons belong to groups and fighters know some: -2 to wield an unfamiliar weapon, -1 to parry one, and -2 in feints and disarms against one unless both sides face the unfamiliar.

unorthodoxWeapons.Name: Unorthodox weapon use
unorthodoxWeapons.Hint: Two-handed weapons in one hand for the strong, melee weapons hurled, and everyday items improvised as weapons.

shovesAndShields.Name: Shoves, slams and shields
shovesAndShields.Hint: Shoves with weapons and shields, cross-checking slams with long weapons, striking at shields and cloaks, and grabbing them.

untrainedFighters.Name: Untrained fighters
untrainedFighters.Hint: Fear and the Coin Toss for those with no combat skills or Combat Reflexes; Committed and Defensive Attack, Feints, Deceptive Attacks, Rapid Strikes and Defensive Grips need a melee skill at DX level.

harshRealism.Name: Harsh Realism for Unarmed Fighters
harshRealism.Hint: Bare-handed parries against weapons at -3 with the limb in the way, low-line parries, footwork dives, skull blows that hurt, the off hand, and bruised knuckles.

grapplingOptions.Name: Grappling options
grapplingOptions.Hint: All-Out and Committed Attacks in grappling, one-handed strangles, more actions after a grapple, throws from locks, sprawling, and defense while grappling.

longWeaponsInClose.Name: Long weapons in close combat
longWeaponsInClose.Hint: -4 skill a yard of reach, Parry from that skill and -1 swing damage a yard, and a haft attack for long polearms.

grabAndSmash.Name: Grab and Smash, and pain
grabAndSmash.Hint: All-out grapple and strike, Kiss the Wall, locks and strangles that cause pain instead of injury, and -4 to attack from inside a grapple.

bodiesInClose.Name: Teeth and bodies in close combat
bodiesInClose.Hint: Everyone can bite and hold on, with what a bite reaches set by size; extra arms and legs in grappling.

partialInjuries.Name: Partial injuries
partialInjuries.Hint: Wounds to an arm, leg or the torso start to hurt after 2×HT seconds: DX, Dodge and Move penalties by how bad they are.

extremeDismemberment.Name: Extreme dismemberment
extremeDismemberment.Hint: A cut that severs an arm, hand, leg or foot the victim is using may carry through to the other one.

severeBleeding.Name: Severe bleeding
severeBleeding.Hint: Severed parts, the neck, skull, veins and vitals bleed faster and harder; First Aid takes the same penalty, and some need Surgery.

lastingInjuries.Name: Lasting injuries
lastingInjuries.Hint: A major wound to the neck, skull, veins or vitals rolls on its table for a lasting or permanent effect.

whoDrawsFirst.Name: Who draws first
whoDrawsFirst.Hint: A GM tool settles a standoff between two fighters drawing weapons: Fast-Draw, weapon skill, and who strikes first.

chargingFoes.Name: Charging foes
chargingFoes.Hint: Weapon skill against an evader, striking him for half damage on a win; a foe hurt by a stop thrust must force his way past the weapon or run himself onto it.

stopHits.Name: Stop Hits
stopHits.Hint: A Wait may attack into the foe's attack: both roll to hit, and the one who does worse defends at -1, or -3 parrying with his attacking weapon.

cascadingWaits.Name: Cascading Waits
cascadingWaits.Hint: A GM tool rolls the Quick Contest for several Waits triggering together and posts the order they act in.

matterOfInches.Name: A matter of inches
matterOfInches.Hint: Weapon length and weight in who draws first, Stop Hits and Cascading Waits, and weight in feints, Beats, multiple parries and parrying flails.

chambara.Name: Chambara fighting
chambara.Hint: Masters (Trained by a Master or Weapon Master) leap, trade attacks for steps, retreat for +3 again and again, use acrobatics with every defense, and sense attacks from behind; Flying Leap, Light Walk and Lizard Climb gain their chambara feats.

contestOfWills.Name: Contest of Wills
contestOfWills.Hint: A Concentrate challenges a foe to a turn-by-turn contest of Will; the loser reacts with the margin as a bonus, and attacks the winner at that penalty.

concentration.Name: Concentration
concentration.Hint: Giving in to a distracting disadvantage (not Berserk or Bloodlust) leaves a fighter at -2 DX.

fear.Name: Fear and martial artists
fear.Hint: Gruesome wounds offer the GM a Fright Check without the heat-of-battle bonus, and known victories add to Intimidation of minor NPCs.

fakingIt.Name: Faking it
fakingIt.Hint: Stage Combat defaults to Combat Art and Sport at -2 and to combat skills and Performance at -3; a GM tool rolls a faker against a trained fighter.

unarmedEtiquette.Name: Unarmed Etiquette
unarmedEtiquette.Hint: Weapons and shields can't parry or block unarmed attacks.

shakingItOff.Name: Shaking It Off
shakingItOff.Hint: A PC may spend 1 FP right after a failed knockdown roll to stay standing.

shoutItOut.Name: Shout It Out!
shoutItOut.Hint: A secret style lets a fighter shout one attack (-1 to defend) or defense (+1) per style per battle.

proxyFighting.Name: Proxy fighting
proxyFighting.Hint: Techniques through objects and people: -4, the borrowed part's penalty, or an unwilling puppet's ST/2.

bulletTime.Name: Bullet Time
bulletTime.Hint: A GM tool spends 3 unspent points for one turn in stopped time, against defenseless foes.

tournaments.Name: Tournament combat
tournaments.Hint: A GM tool resolves bouts by Quick Contest (once, per round or per point, with deadly hits) or by the detailed method's lulls, flurries and presses.

Committed.Title: Committed Attack
Committed.NoDodge: No dodge after a Committed Attack kick
Committed.NoBlock: No block with the shield that made the Committed Attack
Committed.NoRetreat: No retreat after a Committed Attack
Committed.NoFeverish: No Feverish Defense after a Committed Attack

Benefits.kick: Kick: +2 against Leg Grapple and to stay standing

Long.Title: Long
Long.CrouchRoll: Ending the Long attack in a crouch

Slam.NotThisOption: A slam at full Move takes Determined, Feint or Strong

Move.SlamDamage: Thrusts use slam damage when better
Move.NoDodge: No dodge after striking with a leg, head or body on Move and Attack
Move.NoBlock: No block with the shield that struck on Move and Attack
Move.NoRetreat: No retreat after a Move and Attack
Move.NoRapidStrike: No Rapid Strike on Move and Attack
Move.NoDeceptive: No Deceptive Attack on Move and Attack

Acrobatics.Title: Acrobatics
Acrobatics.Hint: A stunt makes your next dodge an Acrobatic Dodge: +2 if it worked, -2 if not. The number is the yards moved, the footing penalty, further bounces or repeats, as the stunt needs.
Acrobatics.StandHint: Acrobatics-6, less encumbrance: up from lying, or up as a step from sitting or crawling
Acrobatics.NoAcrobatics: Acrobatic Stand needs the Acrobatics skill
Acrobatics.InputHint: Yards moved, footing penalty, further bounces or repeats
Acrobatics.OneOrOther: An attack is either acrobatic or flying
Acrobatics.NoDefenseAllOut: No active defenses after an all-out Acrobatic Stand

Note.asStep: Up, and that counts as the step of your maneuver
Note.turnOver: Up, but your turn is over
Note.fellFlying: The leap failed: you fall, and don't attack

Posture.Title: Posture
Posture.CantDropFromHere: Not a drop you can make from this posture
Posture.FaceUpHint: Face-up or prone: the Martial Arts posture tables treat them differently

Feint.Title: Martial Arts feints
Feint.BeatLanded: Beat: {foe}'s {defense} is at {penalty} until the end of your next turn
Feint.DefensiveLanded: Defensive feint: {foe}'s next attack on you is at {penalty}

Readying.Title: Readying weapons
Readying.ReadyHint: One Ready draws, changes reach, hands and grip, and regains control
Readying.RapidHint: Weapon skill at -4 two-handed, -6 one-handed, unpenalized with a tonfa; not to or from a Defensive Grip
Readying.RapidOnlyReversed: A rapid grip change is between a regular and a Reversed Grip
Readying.RapidDropped: Failed: the weapon is dropped, and the turn is over
Readying.RapidCritical: Critical failure: a Tip Slash to your torso, and the weapon is dropped

Sources.floorFlip: From the floor, with a foot

Readying.QuickFailed: Failed: the turn is spent clutching at air
Readying.QuickCritical: Critical failure: the weapon is knocked 1d yards away (on an 18, it hurts)
Readying.TurnOver: The draw failed, and no more are possible this turn
Readying.DroppedAll: Critical failure: the weapon (or all of them) is dropped
Readying.DefensiveNeedsReady: Drawn: getting into a Defensive Grip still takes a Ready

Carries.sameHip: Hip, same side as the weapon hand

Grips.DefensiveHint: One-handed: -2 to hit, +1 damage, counts as two-handed. Two-handed: swings -2 damage (or -1 per die), -1 to breakage, Wild Swings -2 more. +1 to parry from the front, -1 more from the side.
Grips.HalfSwordHint: Reach C, thrusts only, and 2 less off the chinks-in-armor penalty.
Grips.ReversedHint: Reach shortened, thrusts +1 damage, swings -2 (or -1 per die), parry -2. Feints and Deceptive Attacks to the front or sides give -1 more to defend.
Grips.ForearmNone: A forearm parry needs Brawling or Karate and a reach C or 1 weapon in a Reversed Grip
Grips.ForearmFailed: Failed forearm parry: the attacker may choose to strike the weapon instead.
Grips.TelegraphicDeceptive: A Telegraphic Attack can't be a Deceptive Attack

Styles.Title: Styles
Styles.Together: All styles together: points spent / cost
Styles.NotAll: not every style is known yet
Styles.OverPerks: More Style Perks than the allowance
Styles.None: No Style Familiarity a style template describes.
Styles.CinematicWithoutSpark: Cinematic ({skills}) without Trained by a Master or Weapon Master

Training.Title: The Training Sequence
Training.Label: The Training Sequence: {style}

Reasons.spark: Trained by a Master or Weapon Master

Training.StudentFails: doesn't qualify (attributes, or the style's skills at 16+)
Training.Critical: critical failure: the master's worst attack strikes this student
Training.Allowance: may spend up to {points} earned points on what was taught
Training.AllowanceFree: may spend up to {points} earned points on what was taught, and gains {free} free point

Weapons.Title: Weapon build
Weapons.BalanceHint: Cheap: -60% and -1 to skill (or Acc for missile weapons). Fine: +400% and +1 (not sticks or improvised weapons).
Weapons.AccessoriesHint: Combination-weapon accessories: each adds its cost, weight and an attack mode; +1 ST per lb. (per 2 lbs. two-handed); a kusari makes the weapon two-handed.

Disguise.cap: Capped pole weapon (+$30, or $150 presentation; +0.5 lb.)
Disguise.sheathed: Sheathed inside an item (×3 cost, a grade lower)

Weapons.TrickHint: Deploying it takes a DX roll. Strapped on: -1 to skill in melee; a missile weapon has Acc 0 and gets no Aim bonus.
Weapons.HoldoutLine: Holdout: {penalty} for the weapon, +{bonus} from rigs, trick mechanism and clothing.
Weapons.DisguisedSearch: Disguised: finding it takes a Search roll, not Holdout.

earLost.Title: Ear cut
earLost.Text: {name}'s ear is cut; injury past HP/4 was lost. It counts as a major wound, without the face's -5 to knockdown.

earRemoved.Title: Ear lost
earRemoved.Text: {name}'s ear is cut off: a major wound, and a level of Appearance lost.

noseBroken.Title: Broken nose
noseBroken.Text: {name}'s nose is broken: a major wound to the face, and No Sense of Smell/Taste until it heals.

noseLopped.Title: Nose lopped off
noseLopped.Text: {name}'s nose is cut off: two levels of Appearance lost.

spineCrippled.Title: Crippled spine
spineCrippled.Text: {name}'s spine is crippled: automatic knockdown and stunning, Bad Back (Severe) and Lame (Paraplegic), each with its own recovery roll.

jointCrippled.Title: Crippled joint
jointCrippled.Text: {name}'s joint is crippled; recovery rolls are at -2.

MultipleAttacks.UseOwnRapidStrike: Use the Martial Arts Rapid Strike option below

Refusals.oneSpecial: Only one of Rapid Strike, Combination or Dual-Weapon Attack per maneuver
Refusals.noRapidOnMove: No Rapid Strike on a Move and Attack
Refusals.alreadyRapid: This turn's Rapid Strike is already under way
Refusals.noRapidHere: No Rapid Strike with this attack

MultipleAttacks.Skipped: Skipping {skipped} yard(s) between targets uses up {skipped} attack(s)
MultipleAttacks.TooFar: Skipping {skipped} yard(s) to that target would use up the attacks left
MultipleAttacks.RepeatedGrapple: The same grappling move can't be repeated on this foe this turn

Defenses.Locked: Used in a Cross or Supported Parry this turn
Defenses.RetreatAlready: A retreat option replaces Retreat: untick one
Defenses.RiposteFloor: A Riposte can't take the Parry below 8
Defenses.RipostePending: Riposte: -{penalty} on {foe}'s defense against your next attack with that weapon
Defenses.WaitParried: This unbalanced weapon parried during the Wait, and can't attack in it
Defenses.LegOnly: A leg parry defends only the feet, legs and groin
Defenses.LegNoRetreat: No retreat in a turn you parried with a leg
Defenses.LegHit: Failed leg parry against a weapon: the attacker may strike the leg instead.
Defenses.DualFailed: Failed: both halves of the Dual-Weapon Attack hit.
Defenses.Evasive: Evasive movement (against the shooter you target at the end of your turn)
Defenses.NoEvasive: Dodging firearms takes evasive movement against this shooter

Techniques.TaName: Name it TA (Skill Attack/Target), e.g. TA (Broadsword Swing/Neck)
Techniques.ComboName: Name it Combination (Skill Attack/Target + Skill Attack/Target), with two or three attacks
Techniques.ComboMissing: A Combination needs every attack's skill
Techniques.ComboUnusable: Without Trained by a Master or Weapon Master, a three-attack Combination needs 5 points spent on it
Techniques.NoMove: No Combination on a Move and Attack
Techniques.OneSpecial: Only one of Rapid Strike, Combination or Dual-Weapon Attack per maneuver
Techniques.AimAt: This attack of the Combination is aimed at the {target}
Techniques.ComboDefended: Combination: an attack missed or was defended

Effort.GiantStepNote: Giant Step: an extra step before or after the attack
Effort.GreatLungeNote: Great Lunge: +1 reach, swings -2 damage (or -1 per die), defenses kept
Effort.HeroicChargeNote: Heroic Charge: no Move and Attack penalty or cap; its defense limits still apply

Refusals.oneOffense: Only one offensive extra-effort option a turn
Refusals.oneDefense: Only one defensive extra-effort option a turn
Refusals.defensiveGrip: No Great Lunge from a Defensive Grip
Refusals.mightyAttackOnly: Mighty Blows only on an Attack maneuver

Effort.FlurryWithoutRapidStrike: Flurry of Blows needs a Rapid Strike: no FP spent

Ranged.WithFastDraw: Roll {skill} first, for a shot this turn with nothing drawn
Ranged.UnderFireHint: In combat in a realistic game: -4 to the Fast-Draw and readying rolls.
Ranged.ArrowDropped: The ammunition is dropped: the turn is spent on a Ready
Ranged.TooSlow: Readied too slowly to shoot this turn; it can shoot on a later turn at no penalty
Ranged.ShootNow: {weapon} is ready: its next shot this turn is at {penalty}
Ranged.PredictionTooLow: A prediction shot needs effective skill {minimum} or better; this shot is at {skill}
Ranged.FeintOutOfRange: The target is {yards} yards away, past this weapon's range of {range}
Ranged.ReadyInHand: One hand holds {ready} ready: the rest of these {attacks} throws are readied as the Rapid Strike goes, one Ready or Fast-Draw each

Unorthodox.UnfamiliarHint: A weapon from outside the groups this fighter knows: {penalty} to skill
Unorthodox.FamiliarHint: The weapon groups this fighter has trained with or against, separated by commas. A weapon with no group is familiar to everyone.
Unorthodox.GroupHint: The group this weapon belongs to, e.g. a culture. Fighters who don't list it wield it at -2 and parry it at -1.
Unorthodox.OneHandHint: A two-handed weapon in one hand: {skill}, -1 damage
Unorthodox.NowOneHand: {weapon} is now wielded in one hand
Unorthodox.NoBase: No {base} in the compendia to improvise from

Shields.Title: Shields
Shields.WeaponShove: Shove with a weapon or shield
Shields.LongShove: Shove two foes with a long weapon
Shields.NeckNote: At the neck: crushing damage there counts as to the neck
Shields.GrabHint: Grab the targeted foe's shield or cloak: DX or a grappling skill at -4 plus its DB. Held, it gives no Block or DB until they break free.
Shields.OneTarget: Target the one foe whose shield you grab
Shields.NoShield: {name} has no shield or cloak ready
Shields.BreakFreeLabel: {name} breaks free of the shield grab

Untrained.FearText: {names}: no combat skills or Combat Reflexes. Fright Check at +{bonus} for the heat of battle, or drop weapons and flee.
Untrained.CoinAttack: {name} rolls {roll}: All-Out Attack (Determined) on the nearest threat
Untrained.CoinDefend: {name} rolls {roll}: All-Out Defense (Increased Dodge), backing away
Untrained.Limited: Needs a melee combat skill at DX level or better (an Art or Sport skill at DX+3)
Untrained.LimbHit: {name}'s parry failed by 3 or less: the blow lands on the parrying arm
Untrained.BruisedFullPower: Strike the hurt part at full power
Untrained.BruisedIgnored: High Pain Threshold: the hurt part doesn't matter
Untrained.BruisedFull: Full power with a hurt part: shock {shock} again
Untrained.BruisedFullLow: Full power with a hurt part: shock {shock} again, and a Will roll at {shock} or the blow is pulled anyway

CloseCombat.SprawlReady: {name} will sprawl against the next takedown
CloseCombat.SprawlWorked: {foe} sprawled: {taker} falls too and loses the grapple
CloseCombat.SatOnText: {name} sits on {foe}: hands free, and {foe} breaks free against +5
CloseCombat.Shoved: {name} moves {foe}: behind, around, or a step in any direction
CloseCombat.ThrowStanding: Only a standing foe can be thrown from a lock
CloseCombat.Breakfall: {foe} breakfalls: down, but not thrown for damage
CloseCombat.LetGoToRetreat: Let go with every limb to retreat
CloseCombat.InCloseHint: A long weapon in close combat: {skill} skill, {parry} Parry, less swing damage
CloseCombat.BearHugAsk: Squeeze {foe}: crush the breath out of him for fatigue, or squeeze for injury?

BearHug.torso: A bear hug squeezes a torso, not another body part
BearHug.hands: A bear hug takes two arms, or the legs
BearHug.size: Your Size Modifier must exceed his, or he must weigh no more than your Basic Lift x4 for fatigue

CloseCombat.SwitchedToLegs: The grapple is held with the legs now; the hands are free.
CloseCombat.SwitchedToArms: The grapple is held with the arms now.
CloseCombat.ActionManeuver: An action after a grapple takes an Attack, All-Out Attack or Committed Attack maneuver
CloseCombat.ActionUsed: That is this turn's action after a grapple; All-Out Attack (Double) allows two
CloseCombat.OneHandedCrook: With the crook of an arm (-4)
CloseCombat.OneHandedNote: Damage rolls and throws from the lock are at -4, and ST-based effects use half ST
CloseCombat.ChokedUp: The {weapon} is choked up around the head.
CloseCombat.HaftOnlyHint: In close combat this weapon only does quarterstaff damage with its haft until a Ready chokes it up

GrabSmash.KissSlip: Kiss the wall: slipped, into your own face
GrabSmash.PainHint: The points the lock or hold would have done: they become pain instead (2-3 moderate, 4-5 severe, 6-9 terrible, 10+ agony).
GrabSmash.PainChokes: Strangling from now on causes pain, not injury
GrabSmash.BiteCantReach: A bite this size can't reach that
GrabSmash.WorryNoBite: There is no bite to worry with
GrabSmash.WorryCap: Injury to this part is capped at {cap}
GrabSmash.TwoferNote: {victim} may defend: the body coming at him counts as a weapon weighing {weight} lbs. If he defends, neither fighter is hurt.
GrabSmash.HorizontalNo: A horizontal body cannot make that attack: {attack}
GrabSmash.Diffuse: {foe} is diffuse: there is nothing to hold
GrabSmash.Homogenous: {name} is homogenous: the lock tears nothing to injure
GrabSmash.Spines: {foe} has spines: {name} takes damage for holding on.

RamTogether.DualWeapon: A second grapple this turn (Dual-Weapon Attack)
RamTogether.RamNote: {first} and {second} may each defend. If both fail, each takes the blow.

Injury.CarryAsk: {attacker}'s cut severs {victim}'s {part}. Carry it through to the other one?

Partial.armWill: Badly wounded arm: {dx} DX with it, and a Will roll ({will}) to use it at all
Partial.leg: Wounded leg: {dx} DX to kick with it
Partial.legWill: Badly wounded leg: {dx} DX to kick with it, and a Will roll ({will}) to use it at all

Injury.NoSurgery: The surgeon has no Surgery skill
Injury.LastingResult: {victim}, {table} wound (rolled {rolls}): {effect}, {duration}. The GM adds it if it applies: a trait can be dragged from the compendium onto the character.

Timing.LengthHint: Where the weapon sits among weapons of the same Reach.

Draw.Title: Who draws first
Draw.Pick: Select one fighter's token and target the other, or target both
Draw.NoWeapon: Each fighter needs a weapon or a bare-handed attack
Draw.OtherHint: Posture, a grapple, moving and where the weapon is carried are applied for you; add anything else here.
Draw.Label: Who draws first: {a} and {b}
Draw.BothReady: Both weapons are ready: the turn sequence decides.
Draw.Simultaneous: They attack at the same moment: each may dodge or block, but not parry.
Draw.ThrowsAway: {name} throws the weapon away, and {foe} strikes first!

StopHit.Pick: Target the foe the Stop Hit is against
StopHit.Armed: {name} attacks into {foe}'s attack: both roll to hit before either defends.
StopHit.OnlyThatFoe: This weapon can only parry the foe of the Stop Hit
StopHit.ParriedAlready: This weapon parried as part of the Stop Hit, and can't parry again

Waits.Title: Cascading Waits
Waits.Pick: Target the waiting fighters (two or more)
Waits.Together: at the same moment; they can't parry with the weapons they attack with

Charging.Impaled: If {victim} was closing on {attacker}, the {weapon} is inside him. He can spend two movement points to back off and change paths, or run himself onto it.
Charging.InTheWay: If {victim} was closing on {attacker}, the {weapon} is in the way. He must win a Quick Contest of ST to get closer, or spend two movement points to sidestep.
Charging.IfKnockedDown: If the knockdown roll failed, he falls, stunned, and his turn ends.
Charging.Knockback: Knocked back {yards} yards: he must use more movement to close the gap.
Charging.PassesThrough: {victim} takes {injury} more injury. His thrust with the weapon (up to {max}) beats DR {dr}: it comes out his back as he moves in, and it's stuck.
Charging.Stuck: {victim} takes {injury} more injury, but his thrust with the weapon (up to {max}) doesn't beat DR {dr}: he can't come further.

Chambara.Title: Chambara
Chambara.Jumps: Jumps: {high} in. high and {broad} ft. broad standing; {runningHigh} in. and {runningBroad} ft. running
Chambara.NoFullLeap: Needs Acrobatics and Jumping at DX or better to leap full distance in combat
Chambara.TradeStep: Trade an attack for a step
Chambara.NoTrade: No basic attack left to trade for a step
Chambara.Traded: {name} trades an attack for a step: {steps} steps this turn
Chambara.NoFatigue: Success by 5 or more: no FP spent
Chambara.TargetFoe: Target the foe whose weapon you leap onto
Chambara.NoFoeWeapon: The foe has no melee weapon ready
Chambara.StoodOnAsk: If {foe} fails to defend, {name} is standing on the {weapon}.
Chambara.StoodOn: {weapon} stood on: -4 to hit with anything else
Chambara.CantUse: Someone is standing on the {weapon}: take a Ready to dump them off
Chambara.Cling: Lizard Climb: cling to the wall
Chambara.Falls: The climber falls, and the turn ends

Lizard.bonus: Climbing upward: +1 more to the next retreat
Lizard.automatic: Critical success: the next defense succeeds automatically
Lizard.fails: The climb failed: the next defense fails
Lizard.criticallyFails: The climb critically failed: the next defense critically fails

Chambara.NeedsAcrobaticsJumping: Needs Acrobatics and Jumping at DX or better
Chambara.NeedsTechnique: Needs a point in an offensive technique
Chambara.TickRetreat: Tick Retreat to retreat more than a step
Chambara.BeyondMove: Retreats this turn can't go past Move {move}
Chambara.NeedsMoveAndAttack: The acrobatic and flying versions are a Move and Attack
Chambara.NeedsWildSwing: Tick Wild Swing for the spinning version

Wills.AlreadyRefused: {foe} already refused this challenge this combat
Wills.Title: Contest of Wills
Wills.RefuseRoll: Will: refuse the Contest of Wills
Wills.Reaction: {loser} reacts: {rolled} +{bonus} = {total}, {reaction} (potential combat). Attacking {winner} anyway: {penalty} to hit.

Status.running: {challenger} and {foe} are locked in a Contest of Wills.
Status.over: The Contest of Wills between {challenger} and {foe} is over.

Fear.Title: Gruesome wound
Fear.Text: {name} may need a Fright Check, without the +5 for the heat of battle.
Fear.DefeatedHint: Minor NPCs who know of these victories: +1 to Intimidation per five, to +4

Faking.Title: Faking it
Faking.Pick: Select or target the faker, and target a trained fighter watching (if any)
Faking.Label: {name} fakes martial arts

Cinematic.Etiquette: Unarmed Etiquette: no weapon or shield against an unarmed attack

Shake.Title: Shaking It Off
Shake.Text: {name} may spend 1 FP to shake off the failed knockdown roll.
Shake.Done: {name} shakes it off and stays standing.
Shake.TextConscious: {name} may spend 1 FP to shake off the failed roll to stay conscious.

Bullet.Title: Bullet Time
Bullet.Pick: Select or target the character entering Bullet Time
Bullet.Ask: Spend {cost} unspent character points for {name} to take one turn in stopped time?
Bullet.NotSuggested: The book suggests Bullet Time only for Enhanced Time Sense, Trained by a Master or Weapon Master.
Bullet.Text: {name} acts in stopped time: foes are defenseless, and a step makes paused attacks miss.

Shout.Unmarked: {style} is no longer a secret style
Shout.OverLimit: More secret styles than the GM's limit of {allowed} (one per 50 points)
Shout.AllUsed: Every secret style has been shouted this battle

Proxy.TooFar: A proxy reaches at most {yards} yards
Proxy.NeedGrapple: Grapple the proxy with both hands from behind first
Proxy.NeedTarget: Target the person to slap into the foe
Proxy.Outskilled: Your best melee skill must beat the proxy's
Proxy.ObjectNote: Through an object: no heavier than Basic Lift (1/10 for suspended or rolling ones)
Proxy.SlapNote: If the proxy fails to defend, the borrowed part strikes the foe; the proxy is unharmed
Proxy.PuppetNote: Damage is unchanged; a parry that would hurt you hurts the proxy
Proxy.Weight: Proxy object's weight (lbs.; 1/10 if suspended or rolling)
Proxy.TooHeavy: The object weighs more than your Basic Lift ({bl} lbs.)

Tournament.Title: Tournament bout
Tournament.Pick: Select one fighter's token and target the other, or target both
Tournament.NoSkill: {name} has no skill for this competition ({kinds})
Tournament.Clock: {phase}: {left} s left in it ({elapsed}/{total} s, {remaining} s to go)
Tournament.PressFailed: {name} fails to press: a lull begins
Tournament.FatigueTaken: Fatigue for the round: {fp} FP each
